svg.title: Why lowering the pH dissolves calcium fluoride
svg.desc: The dissolving equilibrium CaF2 solid in equilibrium with calcium ion and two fluoride ions. Added hydronium reacts with fluoride, the conjugate base of the weak acid HF, to form HF and water. Removing fluoride lowers Q below Ksp, so more solid dissolves. A second panel shows silver chloride: chloride is the conjugate base of a strong acid, does not react with hydronium, so its solubility does not change with pH.

g.text: F⁻ is removed → Q < Ksp → more CaF₂ dissolves (Le Châtelier).
Cl⁻ comes from a strong acid, HCl: it does not take H⁺ from H₃O⁺, so pH has no effect.
